approved: Parliamentary Business Resources Legislation Amendment (Machinery of Government Change) Bill 2025
Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record

This bill would delay a machinery of government change that transfers administration of certain parliamentary resources from the Department of Finance to the Independent Parliamentary Expenses Authority.

It would amend the commencement provision of the Parliamentary Business Resources Legislation Amendment (Review Implementation and Other Measures) Act 2024 to move the start date from 1 July 2025 to 1 July 2026.

The delay is intended to reduce disruption after the 2025 federal election and give IPEA time to settle its administration before the next statutory review of the Parliamentary Business Resources Act 2017 in late 2027.
Delays the transfer of administration of certain resources under the Parliamentary Business Resources Act 2017 from the Department of Finance to the Independent Parliamentary Expenses Authority.
Delays the extension of IPEA's ruling function, protection from liability for incorrect personal advice, and exemption under the Freedom of Information Act 1982 for personal advice provided by IPEA.
Amends the commencement date for Schedule 1 of the PBR Amendment Act from 1 July 2025 to 1 July 2026.
The Department of Finance, the Independent Parliamentary Expenses Authority, and parliamentarians and their staff who would receive advice and support after the 2025 federal election.

Moved procedural arrangements to sequence debate and votes on Supply Bills, the Transport Security Amendment Bill 2024, the Parliamentary Business Resources Legislation Amendment Bill 2025 and the Environment Protection and Biodiversity Conservation Amendment Bill 2025. Said the motion was needed because Senate estimates would prevent later consideration.

Moved the Parliamentary Business Resources Legislation Amendment (Machinery of Government Change) Bill 2025, which will delay transferring certain parliamentary resource administration from the Department of Finance to the Independent Parliamentary Expenses Authority from 1 July 2025 to 1 July 2026 to reduce disruption after the 2025 election.

Reported that debate time had expired under an earlier resolution and put the questions required to complete consideration of the listed bills; the question was agreed to and the bill was read a second time.

Moved and amended a Senate business motion setting meeting hours, ordering consideration and expedited voting on listed bills, providing for valedictory statements and budget responses, allowing divisions after 6.30 pm, and adding further bills before the motion was agreed to.
